chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who passes by a well while he does not have a bucket with him. He said: “It is not upon him to descend into the well. Surely the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth, so let him perform tayammum.”

key_terms.أَنْ يَنْزِلَ: to go down into the well in order to access water
key_terms.الرَّكِيَّةِ: a well from which water may be drawn
key_terms.دَلْوٌ: a bucket used to draw water
key_terms.رَبَّ الْمَاءِ: the Lord of water, meaning Allah as the creator and disposer of it
key_terms.رَبُّ الْأَرْضِ: the Lord of the earth, indicating the legitimacy of tayammum with earth
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: so let him perform tayammum as the prescribed substitute for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: If someone finds a well but has no bucket to draw water, should he do wudu or tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding tayammum when water is present but cannot be reasonably accessed. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that a person is not obligated to descend into a well without the necessary means to draw water. Since Allah is the Lord of both water and earth, tayammum is permitted in such a circumstance.
